three_layer_separation.warning: These three layers must not be collapsed. The Library does not become the observer's history, the observer's history does not become the Library, and the coherent continuation space does not become the totality itself.

content.scope_boundary: The axiomatic floor ends before physical interpretation. It establishes a formal architecture from distinction to formal closure, from closure to static maximal totality, from maximality to the absence of privileged worldlines, from whole-Library relationality to arbitrary admissible reference, from observer-relative resolution to relational coherence, from coherence to accessibility and continuation, and from restricted continuation to navigation. The next step is therefore not to add another foundational primitive or to generate a new Library state, but to investigate what mathematical structure can be built on the coherent continuation space already defined.
content.handoff: The primer ends at navigation. Subsequent NSFG research may investigate the geometry, dynamics, topology, symbolic representation, or physical interpretation of coherent navigation, provided it preserves the distinction between the static Library \(\mathcal{M}\) and observer-relative traversal over \(\mathcal{M}\). Downstream models may introduce additional assumptions, but those assumptions must remain downstream and must not be retroactively inserted into the axiomatic floor.
content.poetic_cypher: The whole is everywhere; coherence follows wherever the reference falls.
content.cypher_explanation: The final cipher compresses the revised dependency architecture. 'The whole is everywhere' represents the static, maximally complete Library and its lack of a privileged worldline or exterior. 'Coherence follows wherever the reference falls' represents the requirement that an admissible observer-relative reference can establish a coherent continuation without changing Library membership. The observer's reference determines the currently experienced coherent structure, while the totality remains unchanged. The cipher therefore distinguishes the unchanged ontological totality from the relational traversal through it and introduces no additional primitive.

appendix_A.title: Mathematical Reference Sheet
appendix_A.subtitle: Canonical Definitions, Notation, and Dependency Vocabulary
appendix_A.purpose: Provide the complete mathematical vocabulary required to reconstruct the formal content of the primer without consulting external material. This appendix is normative for notation and formal definitions. It does not introduce new axioms, physical assumptions, or downstream NSFG mechanisms.
appendix_A.scope: The reference sheet specifies the formal domain, primitive XOR operation, generating configurations, XOR closure, observer structure, observer-relative resolution, distinguishability, persistence, coherence, accessible reality, continuation spaces, survivorship, navigation, and the resulting observer-relative graph structure.
appendix_A.notation_rule: Symbols defined in this appendix are canonical for the primer. Interpretive prose may use descriptive language, but mathematical statements should use these definitions unless a later document explicitly extends or refines them.

axiomatic_status.axiom: A_⊕ : ⊕ is the primitive operation of distinction.
axiomatic_status.important_constraint: All other entries in this appendix are definitions, constructions, or consequences of the axiom together with ordinary mathematical inference.

formal_domain.definition: A minimal formal domain containing the configurations required for the primitive operation ⊕ to have operands.
formal_domain.constraint: D is not physical space, spacetime, matter, energy, information, or any other physical ontology.

generators.definition: A specified subset of D containing the configurations from which the XOR closure is generated.
generators.interpretation: G identifies the required generating configurations for the formal closure. It is not an additional primitive operation or physical axiom.

xor.interpretation: XOR is treated at the axiomatic floor as distinction. Equal configurations cancel; unequal configurations produce distinction.

closure.definition: The smallest subset 𝓜 of D containing G and closed under ⊕.
closure.minimality_condition: If S ⊆ D is closed under ⊕ and G ⊆ S, then 𝓜 ⊆ S.
closure.important_constraint: The Library is a set closed under an operation. XOR itself is not a closed set.
closure.interpretation: The Library is generated by closure rather than introduced as an independent ontological primitive.

library.definition: The maximally complete unbounded totality satisfying closure under XOR and self-containment with no definable privileged exterior. 𝓜 is a dimensionally undifferentiated complete relational totality, not a grid, container, temporal sequence, or singularity.

formal_characterization.self_containment: ¬∃ z ∉ 𝓜 such that z is definable within the system using only ⊕ and elements of 𝓜 over D as a privileged exterior
formal_characterization.equivalence: 𝓜 is closed under XOR, self-contained with respect to its formal resources, and contains no privileged definable exterior

library.equation: 𝓜 is defined by property, not by construction: 𝓜 is the maximally complete unbounded totality satisfying XOR closure together with self-containment and absence of a privileged definable exterior. Closure_D describes a property of 𝓜, not a temporal or generative process.
library.self_containment_condition: No element outside 𝓜 is definable within the system as a privileged exterior using the formal resources of the system.
library.whole_library_invariant: At every abstract traversal step, the observer is relationally situated with respect to the entire static Library 𝓜. The observer does not encounter a temporal slice, local neighborhood, generated future, or pre-filtered coherent subset.
library.static_totality_condition: 𝓜 does not change as observer history changes. Changes in observer state, accessibility, distinguishability, or coherent continuation alter the observer's relation to 𝓜, not 𝓜 itself.
library.coherence_membership_separation: Membership in 𝓜 is prior to and independent of observer-relative coherence. Coherence determines whether a traversal relation can be maintained by an observer; it does not determine Library membership.
library.unboundedness_condition: 𝓜 has no privileged boundary, terminal region, or excluded coordinate whose status would determine where coherent traversal is permitted. If an arbitrary x ∈ 𝓜 could function as a coherence boundary merely because of its location in 𝓜, then the totality would possess an observer-independent bound or privileged reference condition inconsistent with its unbounded self-contained definition.
library.no_privileged_origin_condition: No x ∈ 𝓜 is privileged as an ontological origin, reference frame, or starting state. Any x ∈ 𝓜 may serve as the relational origin from which observer-relative coherence is evaluated without becoming the origin or generator of 𝓜.
library.arbitrary_origin_coherence_invariant: For an observer O situated at any arbitrary x ∈ 𝓜, the coherent continuation relation must remain nonempty above the observer's operative coherence threshold. The guarantee is not supplied by x being special, but by the combination of maximal completeness, unboundedness, whole-Library relation, and absence of a privileged exterior reference frame.
library.arbitrary_origin_coherence_formalization: ∀x ∈ 𝓜, ∀O with a defined resolution floor I_N(O), ∃γ ∈ Path(𝓜) such that γ begins at x and 𝓒(γ | O, x) > γ_CO + ε, provided the observer's state admits continuation. No x is excluded from coherent traversal merely by its coordinate within 𝓜.
library.why_arbitrary_origin_is_required: If some x ∈ 𝓜 admitted no coherent continuation solely because of its location, then x would function as a boundary of the unbounded totality or coherence would depend upon a privileged reference frame. Either result would introduce structure external to the relational totality. The absence of a privileged perspective therefore requires coherence to be relocatable: the same relational mechanism must apply from any arbitrary point.
library.whole_library_relation: The observer does not first receive a local subset of 𝓜 and then navigate that subset. At every abstract step the observer is relationally situated with respect to the whole 𝓜. The minimal coherent continuation set emerges only from the relation between that whole totality and the observer's current state, history, and resolution capacity.
library.coherent_continuation_note: For any x ∈ 𝓜, XOR closure ensures that relational operations remain within the Library rather than terminating at an external configuration. The stronger requirement of a nonempty coherent continuation follows from whole-Library traversal together with unboundedness and absence of a privileged reference frame. I_N(O) filters distinguishability and coherence; it does not create, delete, or bound 𝓜.
library.continuation_not_generation: A coherent continuation is not a configuration generated into existence after x. It is an observer-relative traversal relation among configurations already contained in the static totality 𝓜.

library.observer_relocation_invariant: Relocating the observer's relational origin from x to any arbitrary y ∈ 𝓜 does not change the underlying Library or invoke a new external reference frame. Only the observer-relative coherence relation changes.
library.reference_frame_independence: There is no privileged coordinate, state, history, or world line from which coherence is intrinsically defined. Coherence is determined relative to the current observer configuration and history, wherever that observer is situated within 𝓜.
library.noise_without_internal_relation: Viewed from a hypothetical perspective external to 𝓜, the totality need not exhibit the observer-relative structure that appears internally. Such a perspective supplies no useful privileged ordering because the Library's structure is relationally self-contained. The observer-relative coherent world line is therefore not imposed by an external ordering; it emerges from the relation of an observer to the totality itself.

no_privileged_exterior.termination_singleton_is_not_exterior: 𝒵 := {z | z⊕z = z} = {0} ⊂ 𝓜 satisfies ∀x, x⊕x ∈ 𝒵 and 0⊕x = x. 𝒵 is where distinction completes and recursive bounce (x⊕y)⊕y = x degenerates. 𝒵 is a single equivalence class under x∼y ⇔ x⊕y = 0 and is complementary as termination vs generation, not as exterior.
no_privileged_exterior.conclusion: A describable privileged exterior cannot remain external to 𝓜. Any candidate definable using ⊕ and elements of 𝓜 over D is already in 𝓜, including 𝒵.
no_privileged_exterior.scope_constraint: This is a formal boundary condition on describable exteriors concerning absence of privileged internal coherence relation supplied by external God's-eye reference; it does not assert that literal physical exteriority is independently impossible, only that no such reference is definable within the system.

observer.definition: A configuration in 𝓜 capable of maintaining a persistent chain of distinctions above its observer-specific resolution floor.
observer.structural_definition: O is an observer iff O can maintain a persistent chain of distinctions that remain resolvable relative to O.
observer.important_constraint: Observerhood is structural and does not imply consciousness, perception, intention, or agency.

resolution.definition: The minimum effective distinction magnitude observer O can maintain as a stable distinction.
resolution.important_constraint: No universal value of I_N is supplied by the axiomatic floor.

distinguishability.definition: The observer-relative effective magnitude of the distinction between configurations x and y.
distinguishability.non_identity_rule: x ≈_O y does not imply x = y.
distinguishability.non_erasure_rule: x ≈_O y does not imply x ∉ 𝓜.
distinguishability.observer_dependence: The same pair of configurations may be distinguishable relative to one observer and indistinguishable relative to another.

persistence.time_warning: The index i represents abstract ordering and is not yet physical time.
persistence.interpretation: Persistence is the maintenance of observer-resolvable distinctions across an ordered chain.

coherence.binary_condition: 𝓒(γ|O)=1 iff every transition in γ remains resolvable by O.
coherence.interpretation: Coherence is the relation between a path and an observer.
coherence.important_constraint: Prefer 𝓒(γ|O) over 𝓒(γ) whenever observer dependence matters.

accessible_reality.accessible_states: A_O = {x ∈ 𝓜 | ∃γ containing x such that 𝓒(γ|O)=1}
accessible_reality.interpretation: A_O is the subset of the Library accessible through observer-relative coherent traversal.
accessible_reality.non_erasure: x ∉ A_O does not imply x ∉ 𝓜.
accessible_reality.observer_creation_rule: A_O is not ontologically created by O; it is an observer-relative accessibility subset of 𝓜.

continuation.continuation_space: Ω(x) = {γ | γ begins at x and γ is a path contained in 𝓜}
continuation.interpretation: Survivorship restricts observer-accessible continuation without deleting non-surviving paths from the represented continuation space.
continuation.future_generation_rule: The Library does not generate future events. Continuation describes represented paths and their observer-relative survivorship.

survivorship.definition: Observer-relative filtering of continuation paths according to the coherence condition 𝓒(γ|O)=1.
survivorship.interpretation: A path survives relative to O when its transitions remain above O's resolution threshold.
survivorship.deletion_rule: Survivorship does not delete the alternatives contained in Ω(x).

emergent_regularity.definition: A derived relation representing a stable recurring transition across an appropriate family of O-accessible paths.
emergent_regularity.formal_condition: L_O(x,y)=1 iff x→y is a stable recurring transition across an appropriate family of O-accessible paths.
emergent_regularity.probabilistic_form: P_O(y|x) ≈ constant over a defined observer-accessible ensemble.
emergent_regularity.important_constraint: L_O is not an element of the axiomatic set A_N.
emergent_regularity.physical_law_status: No particular physical law is derived by this definition.

navigation.coherent_continuation_set: Γ_O(h_n) = {γ | γ begins with h_n and 𝓒(γ|O)=1}
navigation.interpretation: Navigation is traversal or selection of a continuation within the observer-relative coherent continuation space.

geometry.local_accessible_neighborhood: U_O(x) = {y ∈ 𝓜 | y is reachable from x by an O-coherent path segment}
geometry.interpretation: G_O represents observer-relative relational accessibility among configurations.
geometry.important_constraint: Do not identify G_O with physical spacetime at the foundational stage.

dependency_reference.chain: ⊕ → D → G → Closure_D(⊕,G)=𝓜 → no describable privileged exterior → no universal resolver → persistent distinction → O → I_N(O) → δ_O → 𝓒(γ|O) → A_O=R_O → survivorship → emergent regularity → Γ_O(h_n) → N_O(h_n)
dependency_reference.dependency_rule: A later construction must not be treated as a primitive premise of an earlier construction.
dependency_reference.ordering_principle: Distinction precedes objects; closure precedes accessibility; persistence precedes observerhood; observer-relative resolution precedes coherence; coherence precedes accessibility; accessibility precedes survivorship-based regularity; restricted continuation precedes navigation.

logical_invariants: XOR is the only primitive.
D is the minimal formal domain required for XOR to operate.
G specifies the generating configurations and is not an additional primitive.
The Library is a definition, not an axiom.
A set can be closed under an operation; the operation itself should not be called closed.
The Library is the XOR closure of G within D.
The Library is unfiltered at the axiomatic level.
Existence in the Library is not the same as accessibility to an observer.
Inaccessibility is not erasure.
There is no describable privileged exterior that can remain outside the closure.
There is no observer-independent resolution rule at the axiomatic floor.
I_N is observer-relative.
There is no universal I_N unless an additional axiom is introduced.
Observerhood is structural and is not synonymous with consciousness.
Coherence is relational: 𝓒(γ|O).
Coherence is not an absolute property of a path alone.
The abstract sequence index is not automatically physical time.
The Library does not generate the future.
Survivorship filters accessibility rather than deleting alternatives.
Emergent lawfulness is not an additional axiom.
Navigation is the continuation problem created by observer-relative survivability.
G_O is a relational graph at the foundational stage and is not physical spacetime.
